reasons: Direction is correct: HDI is the service provider (design, development, hosting, maintenance) and the Company/Deerskin is our client, so the inserted warranty and remedy run in our favour.

Cited Section 9 genuinely contains only mutual corporate authority representations plus the Globix acknowledgement — no workmanlike-performance, conformance, legal-compliance or malicious-code warranty and no repair/re-perform/refund remedy — so the clause fails even the 90-day/30-day fallback, and the rule's detection guidance expressly treats a missing express warranty as a deviation to be inserted by redline.

Redline is a clean additive insert as new Section 9(c); it leaves the existing (a) and (b) untouched and tracks the model language while sensibly anchoring conformance to the specifications the Company approves under Section 5.2. Deterministic checks (operation applies; period ≥ 90 days) are satisfied.
Comment is accurate, concise, in our voice, cites the playbook position and offers the 90-day fallback, consistent with tone requirements.

Minor, non-blocking nit: the 12-month conformance period runs from the Effective Date rather than from delivery/launch (Section 1.6), which could start the clock before the Site goes live; worth tightening to 'following launch/acceptance' in negotiation, but this does not undermine the finding.
